packageRules.description: Deny-list compromised axios versions (supply chain attack 2026-03-31)

Automerge everything that does not change what we depend on. lockFileMaintenance only refreshes transitive pins inside the existing constraints, and a rollback returns to a version that already ran here, usually because the newer one was withdrawn - holding either back helps nobody. stabilityDays and internalChecksFilter above still apply, so nothing merges before it has aged and its checks are green.

Mark what a human has to look at, so machinery downstream can tell it apart. A major can break callers; a replacement swaps the dependency for a differently named successor, so the identity of what we depend on changes. Neither is covered by the automerge rule above, but that is a decision only Renovate knows about: nothing on the pull request says which update type it carries, and the auto-merge workflow in netresearch/.github consequently merged them anyway, overriding this policy. The label makes the distinction visible to anything that reads the pull request.
